current_component_sources.quote: A significant result from the gauge work: we found and independently checked a counterexample to a proposed route for giving a lattice gauge model a positive physical interpretation. The calculation shows that one specific, finite, two-dimensional overlap model fails a required positivity test, even after the gauge constraint is accounted for. That rules out that particular shortcut. It does not show that the four-dimensional chiral theory fails, or that its continuum limit is impossible. I’m checking the result against prior research and looking for a construction that avoids the obstruction.

current_component_sources.quote: One precision on the overlap counterexample: the failed test is link-reflection positivity, which is relevant to a standard one-step transfer construction. It does not rule out every possible positive reconstruction, including approaches that group time steps differently. The literature check has not found the same counterexample, but that does not establish priority.

current_component_sources.quote: An update to my last clarification: a second test now indicates that site-reflection positivity also fails for that same finite overlap model, when the original time-resolved gauge observables are retained. The calculation has an interval certificate and an independent numerical and algebraic check; a second full interval rerun is still underway. That weakens the straightforward two-step-transfer escape I mentioned. It still does not rule out a construction using a reduced set of observables, another regulator, or the continuum theory.

current_component_sources.quote: The second interval rerun has now confirmed the site-reflection result. More precisely, the standard two-step explanation cannot reproduce this model’s full time-resolved gauge-observable data. A construction that discards some of those observables could still behave differently, and the four-dimensional chiral theory remains unaffected by this result.
current_component_sources.range_scope: Complete normally visible message 5 of six supplied updates in given order;exact individual time unavailable. Link/site/decimation tests and impurity correction remain distinct,including later completed rerun.

current_component_sources.quote: We tested the most direct reduced-observable escape too: retaining only every second time step. For this same small model at an explicitly specified, extremely weak gauge coupling, it also fails the positivity test after the discarded steps are integrated out. An independent internal audit has checked that calculation. That narrows the possible reconstruction routes, but it still says nothing decisive about other actions, larger groupings of time steps, or continuum unitarity. I’m treating it as a finite-model obstruction, not a failure of the broader chiral programme.
